summary: Independent design_spec_reviewer review of active build-delivery plan revision 4 and the exact current nine-document packet. DSR-01 and DSR-02 are resolved with no remaining material contradiction in the reviewed contracts: UX preserves the established responsive ranges and 120/180/240ms motion; PermissionRequest requires runtimeStateMap for runtime labels, visual state and actions, binds applied allow/deny labels to a matching receipt, and explicitly limits every fixed variant label to static previews. Product scope, bridge authority, no-replay recovery, local diagnostics, ADR state ownership and staged implementation holds remain coherent. Individual source hashes, plan/contract records, registered documents, canonical design_spec document digest and recorded scope-approval bindings match. This is a static specification pass, not implementation or runtime verification. Requested route was gpt-6-astra/high; runtime model/effort identity was not verified.

resolved_findings.resolution: workbench-ux.md now explicitly uses 320–599px, 600–899px and 900px+ ranges and fast 120ms, standard 180ms, panel 240ms. Only easing remains an implementation choice. These match system.md and manifest/CSS motion tokens; the 163-token, 44-variant foundation remains intact.

runtimeStatusContract makes runtimeStateMap mandatory before composing visual variants. Approved behavior requires a matching current-request/current-policy applied receipt and labelByDecision distinguishes allow and deny. USER_DENY and POLICY_DENY use separate labels; expired/cancelled/unknown retain read-only reconciliation; uncertain dispatch never resends. All five variants use previewSampleStatusLabel with static-preview-only markers and mark nested badge labels likewise. Delivery-only approval wording and runtime statusLabel fallback fields are absent. The validator source now checks runtime map authority, preview-only markers and receipt/decision-specific applied labels.

review_evidence.hash_binding_result: All packet document hashes match current bytes and registered artifact records. Contract document/approval records match the packet. Plan and contract hashes match both input and current run metadata. The design_spec document digest matches the ordered contract subset using canonical sorted-key compact JSON. Approval evidence and target hashes match current bytes. Token manifest/CSS and validator were inspected and hashed as supplemental sources; they are not separately included in the design_spec documents digest.
review_evidence.approval_boundary: Recorded user continuation authorizes correction and implementation within approved scope; the approval record explicitly does not claim separate user review of each revised sentence. This review checks recorded scope/target consistency and does not independently attest the underlying conversation identity.
review_evidence.limits: Static document/source review, JSON inspection and SHA256 comparison only. No project validation script, harness command, test, build, package probe, browser/Figma/device interaction, live service call or accessibility execution was performed. Validator behavior was inspected, not executed. This pass proves neither runtime permission/path isolation, SDK compatibility, UI quality, Figma synchronization nor product/release completion. Persistent data location/retention and actual runtime/platform evidence remain held as specified in the plan. No source artifact or run ledger was edited; only this explicitly assigned report file was saved.
review_evidence.next_handoff: Coordinator registers this independent report and obtains the current design_spec handoff, alongside the required plan and product handoffs, before assigning dependent implementation. Keep the staged security, runtime and data-persistence holds in the reviewed plan.
